"'''Happier'''" is a song by American DJ [[Marshmello]] featuring British indie pop band [[Bastille (band)|Bastille]] (mainly the vocals of the band's frontman, [[Dan Smith (singer)|Dan Smith]]). Written by Marshmello, Smith, and [[Steve Mac]], and produced by the former, it was released on August 16, 2018. It reached number two on both the [[UK Singles Chart]] and the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and is the highest-charting single for Marshmello in both the UK and the US (eventually tying with "[[Come & Go (Juice Wrld and Marshmello song)|Come & Go]]" with [[Juice Wrld|Juice WRLD]] on the latter). It is also Bastille's highest-charting single as well on both charts surpassing their 2013 single "[[Pompeii (song)|Pompeii]]"'s number five peak on the Hot 100 and tying at its number two peak on the UK chart. It also logged 27 weeks in the top ten of the Hot 100. The song also currently holds the record for most weeks spent at number one on the [[Dance/Electronic Songs|US Dance/Electronic Songs]] chart, with 69 weeks as of January 2020.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/dance-electronic-songs|title=EDM Music & Dance Songs Chart - Week of January 4, 2020|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=November 26, 2019}}</ref> The song was ranked number 33 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 decade-end chart of the 2010s, becoming the highest-ranking song to not top the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 weekly chart.

The song was performed live at the [[2018 MTV Europe Music Awards]] along with another Marshmello song, "[[Friends (Marshmello and Anne-Marie song)|Friends]]" (with [[Anne-Marie]]).

"Happier" is a song by American DJ Marshmello featuring British indie pop band Bastille (mainly the vocals of the band's frontman, Dan Smith). Written by Marshmello, Smith, and Steve Mac, and produced by the former, it was released on August 16, 2018. It reached number two on both the UK Singles Chart and the Billboard Hot 100 and is the highest-charting single for Marshmello in both the UK and the US (eventually tying with "Come & Go" with Juice WRLD on the latter). It is also Bastille's highest-charting single as well on both charts surpassing their 2013 single "Pompeii"'s number five peak on the Hot 100 and tying at its number two peak on the UK chart. It also logged 27 weeks in the top ten of the Hot 100. The song also currently holds the record for most weeks spent at number one on the US Dance/Electronic Songs chart, with 69 weeks as of January 2020. The song was ranked number 33 on the Billboard Hot 100 decade-end chart of the 2010s, becoming the highest-ranking song to not top the Billboard Hot 100 weekly chart.

The song was performed live at the 2018 MTV Europe Music Awards along with another Marshmello song, "Friends" (with Anne-Marie).

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Dan Smith, frontman of Bastille, had originally written 'Happier' 
for [[Justin Bieber]] but the band ultimately decided to keep it for themselves.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-48066591|title=Bastille's Dan, the marathon man|first=Mark|last=Savage|work=BBC News|date=April 27, 2019|access-date=May 1, 2019}}</ref> "We've been having a great time writing for other artists in and amongst making our Bastille albums and mixtapes," Smith told ''[[NME]]''. "Last year we wrote a song called 'Happier' and everyone got really excited about it so we thought it would be good as a collaboration. We had a really interesting time getting to work on it with Marshmello who managed to find some euphoria in a pretty melancholy, direct song. It's always good to step into somebody else's world for a minute and we're excited to be a part of it."<ref>{{cite news|last=Trendell|first=Andrew|title='Euphoria meets melancholy' – Bastille and Marshmello team up for new song 'Happier'|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bastille-marshmello-team-new-song-happier-2367915|access-date=September 17, 2018|work=NME|date=August 17, 2018}}</ref>

Dan Smith, frontman of Bastille, had originally written 'Happier' 
for Justin Bieber but the band ultimately decided to keep it for themselves. "We've been having a great time writing for other artists in and amongst making our Bastille albums and mixtapes," Smith told NME. "Last year we wrote a song called 'Happier' and everyone got really excited about it so we thought it would be good as a collaboration. We had a really interesting time getting to work on it with Marshmello who managed to find some euphoria in a pretty melancholy, direct song. It's always good to step into somebody else's world for a minute and we're excited to be a part of it."

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: "Happier" is an upbeat [[Pop music|pop]] song that draws elements from [[pop rock]]. Lyrically, the song tells "the tale of a love that's over before one party wants to accept it." ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'''s Kat Bein opined that it "sounds a little more like his radio-forward hits."<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Bein|first=Kat|title=Marshmello and Bastille Bounce Bright On 'Happier': Listen|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8470681/marshmello-bastille-new-song-happier|access-date=September 17, 2018|magazine=Billboard|date=August 17, 2018}}</ref>

sections.heading: Lawsuit
sections.wikitext: In May 2019, Russian [[Trance music|trance]] producer [[Arty (musician)|Arty]] filed a [[lawsuit]] against Marshmello for [[copyright infringement]], citing that "Happier" stole song elements from Arty's remix of the song "[[I Lived]]" by [[OneRepublic]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/marshmello-copyright-lawsuit-arty-onerepublic-bastille-832244/|title=Marshmello Facing Copyright Infringement Lawsuit From Producer Arty|last=Reed|first=Ryan|date=2019-05-07|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=2019-05-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://edm.com/news/arty-marshmello-copyright-lawsuit|title=ARTY is Suing Marshmello and Dan Smith of Bastille for Copyright Infringement|author=EDM com Staff|website=EDM.com|date=6 May 2019 |access-date=2019-05-07}}</ref> According to the suit, it is possible that Marshmello had become familiar with Arty's remix, released in 2014, and had used song elements in his then-upcoming song "Happier," which did not debut until 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youredm.com/2019/05/06/arty-is-suing-marshmello-for-copyright-infringement/|title=BREAKING: Arty Sues Marshmello & Bastille for Allegedly Stealing "Happier"|last=Meadow|first=Matthew|date=2019-05-06|website=Your EDM|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/money/2019/05/06/marshmello-faces-copyright-lawsuit-dj-arty-over-one-republic-remix/1118779001/|title=Producer and DJ Arty sues Marshmello in battle of electronic music heavyweights|website=[[The Tennessean]]|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref> Alongside Marshmello, other defendants in the case include Dan Smith, Steve Mac, and various music publishing companies. Arty is represented by attorney Richard Busch, who had previously represented the [[Marvin Gaye]] family in the "[[Blurred Lines]]" suit.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/happier-a-global-pop-hit-alleged-lawsuit-copy-djs-remix-1207598|title="Happier," a Global Pop Hit, Alleged in Lawsuit to Copy DJ's Remix|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=6 May 2019|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Marshmello's 'Happier' Accused of Ripping Off OneRepublic Remix |url=https://www.billboard.com/thr-esq/happier-a-global-pop-hit-alleged-lawsuit-copy-djs-remix-1207598 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=2019-05-07}}{{Dead link|date=June 2023}}</ref> A federal judge rejected the case in April 2021, stating that Arty had given up ownership of the remix composition in his contract and therefore had no grounds to sue.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maddaus |first=Gene |date=2021-04-09 |title=Marshmello Defeats Arty's Copyright Suit Over 'Happier' |url=https://variety.com/2021/music/news/marshmello-arty-happier-copyright-lawsuit-1234947476/ |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> A federal appeals court later upheld the ruling in March 2022.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Donahue |first=Bill |date=2022-03-18 |title=Marshmello Beats Copyright Case Over 'Happier' at Appeals Court |url=https://www.billboard.com/business/legal/marshmello-wins-copyright-case-happier-arty-appeals-court-1235045947/ |access-date=2024-08-07 |magazine=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref>
sections.text: In May 2019, Russian trance producer Arty filed a lawsuit against Marshmello for copyright infringement, citing that "Happier" stole song elements from Arty's remix of the song "I Lived" by OneRepublic. According to the suit, it is possible that Marshmello had become familiar with Arty's remix, released in 2014, and had used song elements in his then-upcoming song "Happier," which did not debut until 2015. Alongside Marshmello, other defendants in the case include Dan Smith, Steve Mac, and various music publishing companies. Arty is represented by attorney Richard Busch, who had previously represented the Marvin Gaye family in the "Blurred Lines" suit. A federal judge rejected the case in April 2021, stating that Arty had given up ownership of the remix composition in his contract and therefore had no grounds to sue. A federal appeals court later upheld the ruling in March 2022.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
Three music videos were released to support the single. The initially released one was a simple lyric video. This was followed by a performance video featuring Marshmello playing guitar with the bandmembers of Bastille playing their own instruments and Dan Smith singing. At the very end, Smith [[low five]]s Marshmello.{{Citation needed|date=November 2023|reason=various instruments and Dan Smith singing and dancing, both in different frames and only appearing in one at the end of the video.}}

On September 24, 2018, Marshmello released the official music video through YouTube Premiere, starring [[Miranda Cosgrove]] as a teenager who has [[Dental braces|braces]], along with [[Teala Dunn]], Jordyn Jones and James Babson as the father.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Bein|first=Kat|title=Marshmello & Bastille's 'Happier' Video Will Actually Make You Cry: Watch|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/dance/8476511/marshmello-bastille-video-happier|access-date=September 24, 2018|magazine=Billboard|date=September 24, 2018}}</ref> The music video focuses on Cosgrove's character. The color yellow and Marshmello's logo feature throughout the video, but neither he nor anyone from Bastille appear in the video. The video was directed by [[Mercedes Bryce Morgan]] and photographed by cinematographer [[Steve Gainer]].

On September 24, 2018, Marshmello released the official music video through YouTube Premiere, starring Miranda Cosgrove as a teenager who has braces, along with Teala Dunn, Jordyn Jones and James Babson as the father. The music video focuses on Cosgrove's character. The color yellow and Marshmello's logo feature throughout the video, but neither he nor anyone from Bastille appear in the video. The video was directed by Mercedes Bryce Morgan and photographed by cinematographer Steve Gainer.

sections.heading: Synopsis
sections.wikitext: During the main character's 14th birthday party, which is shown to be a disappointment, her father gifts her a yellow bow. This bow is gifted along side a surprise [[Golden Retriever]] puppy, on which the yellow bow was presumably for. As she becomes a teenager, the dog grows along with her. The video cuts some years to high school, where she attempts to join a soccer team but is picked last and shown to be socially rejected. The video contrasts this explicit social exclusion with a shot of her playing soccer with her dog. In the next scene, while posing for a team photo, her teammates push her out from the picture. When she smiles, her teammates see her braces and make fun of her. She runs home and cries, but her dog is there to cheer her up. She tries to play with the dog as usual, but the age of the dog is starting to show and it is revealed that the dog is ill. Months pass, and although the dog is treated with medicine, the dog's illness presumably worsens. The dog is taken to the vet who has a private conversation with the girl's father, to whom he reveals the dog's illness to be terminal. The girl's father explains to his distraught daughter that the dog will need to be [[Animal_euthanasia|euthanized]]. She has an emotional parting exchange, and takes the dog's bow as a keepsake. 20 years later and the girl grows to have a daughter of her own. During her daughter's birthday party, her grandfather similarly gifts her a red bow, and a Golden Retriever puppy. The woman smiles at her daughter's joy and a single tear falls from her eye before she joins her daughter in embracing the new puppy.
